Hunter Valley Rail Infrastructure Group
Operations Manual
Version 4.2 — Updated January 2025

---

1. INTRODUCTION

1.1 Purpose
This manual sets out the standard operating procedures, contact arrangements, shift rosters, and safety protocols for all personnel engaged in rail infrastructure maintenance, inspection, and response activities across the Hunter Valley network. It is the controlling document for day-to-day operations and must be read in conjunction with the Network Rules, the HVRIG Safety Management System, and any corridor-specific instructions issued by the Australian Rail Track Corporation.

1.2 Scope
The provisions of this manual apply to all HVRIG employees, contractors, and visitors while on HVRIG-controlled worksites, in HVRIG vehicles, or when undertaking work on behalf of HVRIG. Where a local instruction or a project-specific plan conflicts with this manual, the more stringent requirement prevails unless an approved deviation has been documented.

1.3 Document Control
This is Version 4.2. It supersedes Version 4.1, which was withdrawn on 31 December 2024. All previous versions are invalid for operational use. A controlled copy of this manual is held by the Operations Manager, the Safety Manager, and the Shift Supervisors’ office at each depot. Uncontrolled copies may be distributed for reference only; any printed copy older than the current version must be destroyed or clearly marked “SUPERSEDED”.

The HVRIG operations manual states that Hunter Valley Rail Infrastructure Group operating_hours are 24/7. Record status: current. This provision is current and applies to all sections of this manual unless a specific clause identifies a limited window.

1.4 Definitions
- HVRIG: Hunter Valley Rail Infrastructure Group
- ARTC: Australian Rail Track Corporation
- TOC: Train Operating Company
- Safeworking: The system of rules and procedures used to protect persons and trains on or about the track
- Possession: A block of track taken out of service for maintenance or construction
- Lookout: A qualified person whose sole duty is to warn track workers of approaching trains

2. EMERGENCY CONTACTS

2.1 Immediate Emergencies
For any incident involving injury, fire, hazardous materials, or risk to life, call 000 first. Then notify the HVRIG Emergency Coordination Line on 1800 555 019. This line is answered at all times, including weekends and public holidays.

2.2 Key Contacts
The following contacts are current as of January 2025. Any changes are to be advised by the Operations Manager in writing.

| Police / Fire / Ambulance | — | 000 | — |

2.3 Duty Officer Roster
A Duty Officer is appointed for each 24-hour period. The roster is published weekly by the Operations Manager and displayed in each depot. The Duty Officer holds the emergency phone and is the first point of escalation for any issue that cannot be resolved by the shift supervisor.

3. OPERATING HOURS AND SHIFT PATTERNS

3.1 General
As stated in Section 1.3, HVRIG operations are continuous. All maintenance, inspection, and response functions are staffed across a 24/7 roster. This means there is always a qualified supervisor, a track patrol team, and a response crew available, regardless of the day or time.
4. COMMUNICATION PROTOCOLS

4.1 General Principles
Clear and timely communication is essential to safe railway operations. All staff are expected to
use the correct communication channel for the type of message being sent, and to confirm that
critical information has been received and understood.

4.2 Radio Communications
Radio is the primary means of communication between track workers, lookouts, and the Shift
Supervisor. The following rules apply:

- All radio calls commence with the call sign of the person being called, followed by the call
  sign of the caller.
- The phonetic alphabet is to be used for all asset and location identifiers (e.g., Tango India
  Victor zero seven for TIV-07).
- Radio messages must be brief and factual. Non-essential conversation is not permitted on
  operational channels.
- When a message is received, the recipient must repeat back the key details (location, time,
  instruction) to confirm accuracy.
- If radio contact is lost or unclear, the person initiating the call must stop work and notify
  the Shift Supervisor immediately. Work shall not resume until reliable communication is
  restored.

4.3 Mobile Phones
Mobile phones may be used for communication where radio coverage is unavailable or where the
message is of a non-urgent administrative nature. All staff are to ensure their issued mobile
phone is fully charged at the start of each shift and carried at all times while on duty.

4.4 Work Groups and Messaging
Each work group has a dedicated messaging channel for day-to-day coordination. These channels are
for operational purposes only. Urgent or safety-critical messages must not be sent by messaging
alone; they must be followed up by radio or phone call to confirm receipt.

4.5 Daily Briefings
A daily briefing is held at the start of each shift at each depot. The briefing covers:

- Work scheduled for the shift
- Any track possessions or speed restrictions in place
- Weather conditions and any associated risks
- Known hazards or incidents from the previous shift
- Any changes to procedures or contact details

Attendance at the daily briefing is compulsory for all staff commencing a shift. Staff who are
unable to attend must contact their supervisor before commencing work.

4.6 Shift Handover
A formal handover is required at the end of each shift. The outgoing supervisor must provide the
incoming supervisor with:

- A summary of work completed and outstanding
- Any incidents or near misses, including follow-up actions required
- The status of any track possessions or speed restrictions
- Condition of plant and equipment, including any faults reported
- Any relevant communications from ARTC Network Control or other external parties

The handover is to be recorded in the shift log and signed by both supervisors.

5. REPORTING LINES

5.1 General
The reporting structure for HVRIG is designed to ensure that issues are escalated promptly to the
appropriate level of authority. Staff are to report to their immediate supervisor in the first
instance, unless the situation is an emergency requiring immediate action.

5.2 Reporting Structure
The following reporting lines apply across all HVRIG operations:

- Track Workers and Lookouts report to the Shift Supervisor.
- Shift Supervisors report to the Maintenance Coordinator for their area (North or South).
- Maintenance Coordinators report to the Operations Manager.
- The Operations Manager reports to the General Manager, HVRIG.
- The Safety Manager has a direct line to the General Manager on all safety matters, and is

Hunter Valley Rail Infrastructure Group
Operations Manual
Version 4.2 — Updated January 2025

---

1. INTRODUCTION

1.1 Purpose
This manual sets out the standard operating procedures, contact arrangements, shift rosters, and safety protocols for all personnel engaged in rail infrastructure maintenance, inspection, and response activities across the Hunter Valley network. It is the controlling document for day-to-day operations and must be read in conjunction with the Network Rules, the HVRIG Safety Management System, and any corridor-specific instructions issued by the Australian Rail Track Corporation.

1.2 Scope
The provisions of this manual apply to all HVRIG employees, contractors, and visitors while on HVRIG-controlled worksites, in HVRIG vehicles, or when undertaking work on behalf of HVRIG. Where a local instruction or a project-specific plan conflicts with this manual, the more stringent requirement prevails unless an approved deviation has been documented.

1.3 Document Control
This is Version 4.2. It supersedes Version 4.1, which was withdrawn on 31 December 2024. All previous versions are invalid for operational use. A controlled copy of this manual is held by the Operations Manager, the Safety Manager, and the Shift Supervisors’ office at each depot. Uncontrolled copies may be distributed for reference only; any printed copy older than the current version must be destroyed or clearly marked “SUPERSEDED”.

The HVRIG operations manual states that Hunter Valley Rail Infrastructure Group operating_hours are 24/7. Record status: current. This provision is current and applies to all sections of this manual unless a specific clause identifies a limited window.

1.4 Definitions
- HVRIG: Hunter Valley Rail Infrastructure Group
- ARTC: Australian Rail Track Corporation
- TOC: Train Operating Company
- Safeworking: The system of rules and procedures used to protect persons and trains on or about the track
- Possession: A block of track taken out of service for maintenance or construction
- Lookout: A qualified person whose sole duty is to warn track workers of approaching trains

2. EMERGENCY CONTACTS

2.1 Immediate Emergencies
For any incident involving injury, fire, hazardous materials, or risk to life, call 000 first. Then notify the HVRIG Emergency Coordination Line on 1800 555 019. This line is answered at all times, including weekends and public holidays.

2.2 Key Contacts
The following contacts are current as of January 2025. Any changes are to be advised by the Operations Manager in writing.

2.3 Duty Officer Roster
A Duty Officer is appointed for each 24-hour period. The roster is published weekly by the Operations Manager and displayed in each depot. The Duty Officer holds the emergency phone and is the first point of escalation for any issue that cannot be resolved by the shift supervisor.

3. OPERATING HOURS AND SHIFT PATTERNS

3.1 General
As stated in Section 1.3, HVRIG operations are continuous. All maintenance, inspection, and response functions are staffed across a 24/7 roster. This means there is always a qualified supervisor, a track patrol team, and a response crew available, regardless of the day or time.

4. COMMUNICATION PROTOCOLS

4.1 General Principles
Clear and timely communication is essential to safe railway operations. All staff are expected to
use the correct communication channel for the type of message being sent, and to confirm that
critical information has been received and understood.

4.2 Radio Communications
Radio is the primary means of communication between track workers, lookouts, and the Shift
Supervisor. The following rules apply:

- All radio calls commence with the call sign of the person being called, followed by the call
  sign of the caller.
- The phonetic alphabet is to be used for all asset and location identifiers (e.g., Tango India
  Victor zero seven for TIV-07).
- Radio messages must be brief and factual. Non-essential conversation is not permitted on
  operational channels.
- When a message is received, the recipient must repeat back the key details (location, time,
  instruction) to confirm accuracy.
- If radio contact is lost or unclear, the person initiating the call must stop work and notify
  the Shift Supervisor immediately. Work shall not resume until reliable communication is
  restored.

4.3 Mobile Phones
Mobile phones may be used for communication where radio coverage is unavailable or where the
message is of a non-urgent administrative nature. All staff are to ensure their issued mobile
phone is fully charged at the start of each shift and carried at all times while on duty.

4.4 Work Groups and Messaging
Each work group has a dedicated messaging channel for day-to-day coordination. These channels are
for operational purposes only. Urgent or safety-critical messages must not be sent by messaging
alone; they must be followed up by radio or phone call to confirm receipt.

4.5 Daily Briefings
A daily briefing is held at the start of each shift at each depot. The briefing covers:

- Work scheduled for the shift
- Any track possessions or speed restrictions in place
- Weather conditions and any associated risks
- Known hazards or incidents from the previous shift
- Any changes to procedures or contact details

Attendance at the daily briefing is compulsory for all staff commencing a shift. Staff who are
unable to attend must contact their supervisor before commencing work.

4.6 Shift Handover
A formal handover is required at the end of each shift. The outgoing supervisor must provide the
incoming supervisor with:

- A summary of work completed and outstanding
- Any incidents or near misses, including follow-up actions required
- The status of any track possessions or speed restrictions
- Condition of plant and equipment, including any faults reported
- Any relevant communications from ARTC Network Control or other external parties

The handover is to be recorded in the shift log and signed by both supervisors.

5. REPORTING LINES

5.1 General
The reporting structure for HVRIG is designed to ensure that issues are escalated promptly to the
appropriate level of authority. Staff are to report to their immediate supervisor in the first
instance, unless the situation is an emergency requiring immediate action.

5.2 Reporting Structure
The following reporting lines apply across all HVRIG operations:

- Track Workers and Lookouts report to the Shift Supervisor.
- Shift Supervisors report to the Maintenance Coordinator for their area (North or South).
- Maintenance Coordinators report to the Operations Manager.
- The Operations Manager reports to the General Manager, HVRIG.
- The Safety Manager has a direct line to the General Manager on all safety matters, and is
